title: A Lean 4 formalization of the master theorem from algorithm analysis
judgment_notes: Big-O notation and the master theorem; course project (Bauer, Ljubljana).

source.citation: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest, Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed., MIT Press 2022 (asymptotic notation, master theorem)
source.evidence: README: course project (Bauer, UL FMF) on Bachmann-Landau notation and the master theorem; blueprint bibliography cites cormen2022, knuth1976, sipser1996, but no "follows" statement; restricted to recurrences on naturals. Page estimate for CLRS Ch. 3 + 4.5-4.6.

edge_sample.source_text: lemma : Let $g$ be asymptotically positive. Then $f$ is not both asymptotically bounded below by $g$ and asymptotically dominated by $g$.
edge_sample.target_text: proof : This is a direct application of Lemma \ref{lemma:not_asymp_pos_bounded_below_and_right_dom}.

edge_sample.source_text: definition : (Big O notation) $f(x) \in O(g(x))$ if it is asymptotically bounded above by $g(x)$.
edge_sample.target_text: lemma : Let $f\_1(x), f\_2(x) \in O(g(x))$. Then $f\_1(x) + f\_2(x) \in O(g(x))$.

edge_sample.source_text: lemma : Let $c < 0$ and let $f$ be asymptotically less than $g$. Then $c \cdot f$ is asymptotically greater than $c \cdot g$.
edge_sample.target_text: proof : Let $k$ be the constant such that $f$ is asymptotically less than $k \cdot g$. By positive scalar multiplicativity of asymptotic inequality, $-c \cdot f$ is asymptotically less than $-c \cdot k \cdot g$. Since $-c \cdot k > 0$, this implies

edge_sample.source_text: lemma : $f$ is asymptotically bounded above by itself.
edge_sample.target_text: proof : This follows directly from Lemma \ref{lemma:asymp_bounded_above_refl}.

edge_sample.source_text: definition : $f$ is asymptotically greater than $g$ if there exists $x_0$ such that $f(x) \ge g(x)$ for all $x \ge x_0$.
edge_sample.target_text: lemma : Let $c < 0$ and let $f$ be asymptotically greater than $g$. Then $c \cdot f$ is asymptotically less than $c \cdot g$.

edge_sample.source_text: theorem : Let $f$ be asymptotically positive. If $f$ is asymptotically bounded below by $g$, then $f$ is not asymptotically dominated by $g$.
edge_sample.target_text: proof : A direct application of Lemma \ref{thm:not_asymp_pos_bounded_below_of_right_dom}.

edge_sample.source_text: lemma : Let $f\_1$ be bounded by $g$. Let also $f\_2$ be asymptotically negative and let $f\_2$ dominate $g$. Then $f\_1 + f\_2$ is bounded by $g$.
edge_sample.target_text: proof : This follows directly from Lemma \ref{lemma:asymp_bounded_add_neg_left_dom}.

edge_sample.source_text: lemma : Let $T$ and $f$ form a lower master recurrence with parameters $(a, n\_0, b, d)$. Then $T(n) \in O(n^{\log_b{a}} + \sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor \log_b{n} \rfloor} (\frac{a}{b^d})^k n^d)$.
edge_sample.target_text: proof : After applying Lemma \ref{lemma:big_o_geom}, we note that $\log_b{a} = d$ and then the proof boils down to showing that the geometric sum is bounded by $\log_b{n}$. Since $\frac{a}{b^d} = 1$, the geometric sum equals $\lfloor \log_b{n} \rfl

edge_sample.source_text: lemma : If $f(x) \in O(g(x))$ and $g(x) \in O(h(x))$, then $f(x) \in O(h(x))$.
edge_sample.target_text: proof : After applying Lemma \ref{lemma:big_o_geom}, we note that $\log_b{a} = d$ and then the proof boils down to showing that the geometric sum is bounded by $\log_b{n}$. Since $\frac{a}{b^d} = 1$, the geometric sum equals $\lfloor \log_b{n} \rfl

edge_sample.source_text: definition : (Big Omega notation) $f(x) \in \Omega(g(x))$ if it is asymptotically bounded below by $g(x)$.
edge_sample.target_text: lemma : Let $f\_1(x) \in \Omega(g(x))$ and let $f\_2$ be asymptotically positive. Then $f\_1(x) + f\_2(x) \in \Omega(g(x))$.
